LEAF ECU

Installation and setup guide for the powertrain controller built around Nissan Leaf components for DIY electric vehicles.

Download PDFContents →
Revision 2.0Date October 202670 figures

1General Information#

Leaf ECU is the master powertrain controller: it drives the inverter and the traction-battery contactors, handles charging through the PDM and CHAdeMO, controls cooling and peripherals, and exchanges data with the BMS, the display and the gear selector over CAN.

1.1Controller Connectors#

The controller has two 24-way connectors:

  • X1 — black;
  • X2 — grey.

Pin numbering is moulded on the connectors: rows A–C and positions 1–8. Pins can be inserted into the mating connector from the back of the housing without taking it apart — just pull out the yellow lock at the front of the connector first.

The pinout is compiled from the wiring diagrams in this manual. The "Diagrams" column lists the figures where the pin is used; hover a pin or a table row to see it on the connector. In the text pins are written as X1-B2 — hover such a tag and the same connector pops up.

1.2Dimensions and Mounting#

The controller is built into an aluminium enclosure with two 24-way connectors. It is fixed with two M6 bolts through the ears on the long sides.

  • The mounting holes lie on one line across the enclosure, 125 mm apart.
  • Leave free space in front of the connector end: the plugs are inserted and removed along the enclosure, and the harness needs room to bend.

1.3CAN Bus#

Warning

All CAN bus wires must be twisted into twisted pairs!

The controller has four CAN buses; the main one is CAN0 Powertrain (X1-A3 / X1-B3), which connects the inverter, the PDM, the OBD2 socket, the display and the selector. The BMS connects to CAN1 (X1-A4 / X1-B4), or to CAN2 (X1-A5 / X1-B5) when CAN1 is used by CHAdeMO.

Every CAN bus must be terminated with 120 Ω at both ends. The controller already has 120 Ω built in on every CAN channel, so the controller sits at one end of the bus and the second 120 Ω must be at the far end. The Leaf inverters also have 120 Ω built in, so CAN0 with a Leaf inverter needs no separate resistors. If the device at the far end has no terminator of its own, fit a 120 Ω resistor next to it. Check: with the bus unpowered, ≈ 60 Ω between CAN-H and CAN-L.

1.4How to Read the Diagrams#

All diagrams in this manual share one style. A wire's colour shows its purpose, not the insulation colour:

Colour Purpose
Traction battery power cables (HV)
+12 V — supply from the battery / vehicle 12 V system
+12 V switched — from the ignition switch or through a relay
+5 V — sensor supply from the controller
Ground
/ CAN-H / CAN-L
Signals into the controller (sensors, buttons, pilot lines)
Controller outputs (relay coils, LEDs)

Relay contacts are numbered 1–2, the coil 4–3: pin 4 receives the drive signal from the controller, pin 3 is ground.

The diagrams use ordinary 30–40 A automotive relays (mini ISO). Their terminals carry the standard numbers: 1 → 30, 2 → 87, 4 → 86, 3 → 85; terminal 87a (changeover relays only) is not used. Click a relay on any diagram to open this connector with the terminal highlighted.

Note

If the relay has a built-in diode or resistor across the coil, coil polarity matters: 86 is "+" (from the controller), 85 is "−" (ground).

In the web edition of this manual the diagrams are interactive: click a wire to highlight the whole circuit and open a card listing its connections; click a pin or a device to open its connector view with the pinout. The Expand button opens a diagram full-screen with zoom.

212 V Power System#

Version 4 controller boards have a new power supply circuit. The controller needs:

  • permanent +12 V from the battery;
  • separately, +12 V from the ignition switch (IGN KEY).

After the ignition key is turned off the controller stays on until the motor stops, then it opens the battery contactors and switches itself off.

The full wiring — 12 V supply, IGN relay, CAN0, PDM, charge inlet, inverter and motor resolver — is given in section 3, separately for each inverter: Fig. 7, Fig. 9, Fig. 11.

Note

The Leaf Type 1 charge inlet has resistor R5 right at the socket, under the rubber boot. It must be relocated and wired as shown in the section 3 diagrams (for example Fig. 9).

The PP line between the PDM and the charge inlet must also be broken: the inlet PP goes to the controller (X1-C7), and the controller drives its own PP signal to the PDM (X1-B7). When a charging gun is plugged into the inlet, the controller wakes up and starts charging.

3Inverter#

To connect the inverter and the PDM it is best to reuse the factory Leaf harness: strip everything unnecessary, keeping the connectors for the inverter, the PDM and the motor resolver.

Every inverter connects to the controller the same way: CAN-H and CAN-L to CAN0 Powertrain (X1-A3 / X1-B3) as a twisted pair, 12 V supply from the IGN relay, ground to the chassis; the resolver and the motor temperature sensor go over the factory harness between the inverter and the motor. A full diagram is given below for each inverter: only the pin numbers differ.

The resolver connector on the motor itself is the same on all three generations — only the inverter-side pins differ:

Note

The inverter's permanent-supply pins (fed from the battery in the factory Leaf wiring) are fed from the IGN relay with the Leaf ECU, like the ignition pin: the controller keeps the relay on until the motor stops.

3.1Leaf Inverter Gen 1 (ZE0)#

Pins 4 and 10 (battery in the Nissan) and 33 (ignition) are the +12 V supply, pins 2 and 8 are ground; CAN-H is 12, CAN-L is 19. The resolver goes to the resolver connector on the motor: 34/35 — excitation R1/R2, 1/6 — S1/S3, 20/27 — S2/S4; motor temperature sensor — 32/31. The old table had the roles of pins 4/10 and 33 swapped; it does not affect the wiring — all three are fed from the IGN relay.

3.2Leaf Inverter Gen 2 (AZE0)#

Pins 46 and 48 (VB1, VB2) and 42 (IGN) are the +12 V supply, pins 47 and 49 are ground; CAN-H is 14, CAN-L is 15. The resolver and the motor temperature sensor run over the factory harness to the resolver connector on the motor: resolver pairs 19/27 (excitation), 20/21 and 18/17, temperature sensor 45/44. The resolver pair shields go to body ground.

3.3Leaf Inverter Gen 3 (ZE1)#

Numbering is Nissan's (harness side of the harness connector). Pins 1 and 6 are the +12 V supply, 18 is ignition (Power ON), 4 and 10 are ground; CAN-H is 5, CAN-L is 11. Resolver: 22/16 — excitation, 19/14 and 3/9 — output windings; motor temperature sensor — 7/20 (all to the resolver connector on the motor); coolant temperature sensor — 12/15.

Warning

Earlier versions of this manual showed a picture with a different numbering of this same connector for Gen 3 (CAN-H 22, CAN-L 17, ground 3/9/16/21). That numbering does not match Nissan's, and it wrongly marks pins 3 and 9 as ground. Use the numbering below.

3.4Tesla Model 3 / Model Y Rear Inverter#

The controller works with the Tesla Model 3 / Model Y rear inverter (Drive Inverter Rear) running the Highland firmware. In the web configurator set Inverter type to Tesla M3 (see 17.3). The controller sends every CAN message the inverter needs by itself — no other Tesla modules are required.

Only the supply, CAN and the resolver are connected to the inverter, through the logic connector X090 (30 contacts):

X090 pin Wire To
3 red (RD) +12 V after the IGN relay
13 black (BK) Ground
12 blue/white (BU/WH) CAN0-H X1-A3
2 blue (BU) CAN0-L X1-B3
26 / 16 yellow / black Resolver: excitation + / − (resolver pins 3 / 8)
17 / 7 green / red Resolver: sine + / − (pins 4 / 9)
8 / 27 violet / blue Resolver: cosine + / − (pins 5 / 10)
10 green (GN) Oil pump, pin 2 (status) — factory harness
  • HVIL and the second CAN (PRTY-CAN) are not connected — pins 4, 23 and 20, 30 stay free, as does Unswitched +12V (22).
  • The accelerator pedal and the brake switch go to the controller, not to the inverter: X090 pins 5, 6, 11, 14, 15, 21, 24, 25 are free.
  • The oil pump stays connected to the inverter as in the car (pin 10 ↔ pump pin 2). The pump supply (pin 1) is +12 V after the IGN relay (in the Tesla the Body Controller switches it), pin 3 is ground. The pump connector pinout is below.
  • The Tesla inverter already has 120 Ω between CAN+ and CAN−, just like the controller — CAN0 needs no separate resistors.

The high-voltage supply (through the contactors, see section 6) goes to the orange HV connector on the inverter cover. Each pole is a pair of blades: the pair by the "−" mark is the battery negative, the pair by "+" the positive. On the Tesla HV cable plug these are cavities 1 (B−) and 2 (B+); the numbers are moulded on the plug.

Danger — high voltage

Reversed HV polarity will damage the inverter. Before closing the contactors for the first time, check with a multimeter that the battery "+" arrives at the blades by the "+" mark. The inverter's own polarity can be checked without the battery with a diode test (as in the Tesla service manual): red probe on the "−" pair, black probe on the "+" pair — the meter reads about 0.45–2.0 V; "OL" means the probes are swapped.

Warning

CAN-H and CAN-L wires must be twisted into a twisted pair.

4PDM Module#

PDM pins 30 and 29 (charge inlet) connect to the two-pin connector on the inlet itself: white wire to white, green to brown (when using the Leaf harness). With the V4 board wire the PP line as shown in the section 3 diagrams (Fig. 9).

The PDM case must be connected to ground — the case is the negative output of the DC-DC converter. The stud on the side of the module is the +12 V output of the DC-DC converter.

4.1Type 1 (J1772) Charge Inlet#

The vehicle inlet and the charging gun are mirror images: on the left of the figure is the inlet (front view, from the side the gun plugs into), on the right the gun (view onto its face). The tag under each connector says which side you are looking at.

Resistor R5 of the stock Leaf inlet (2.7 kΩ) is relocated and wired as shown in the section 3 diagrams (Fig. 9).

4.2Type 2 Charge Inlet#

Type 2 is a three-phase connector; the single-phase Leaf PDM uses only L1, N, PE, CP and PP. With a Type 2 inlet, resistor R5 must be changed to 4.7 kΩ (Fig. 9).

Type 2 cable — 32 A only

With a Type 2 inlet use only a 32 A charging cable (gun) — its plug has a 220 Ω resistor between PP and PE. Cables of other ratings have a different resistor (13 A — 1.5 kΩ, 20 A — 680 Ω, 63 A — 100 Ω) and are not suitable for this wiring.

5Controls#

5.1Selector Buttons#

Driving direction (the selector) can be chosen with buttons or with the original Nissan Leaf selector. The selector type must be set in the web configurator (ECU → Settings, see 17.3).

  • Drive and Reverse buttons — latching.
  • Start button — latching or momentary; its mode is set in the configurator.

How it works:

  1. Pressing Start closes the contactors; the inverter is ready, the selector is in neutral.
  2. To drive off, switch on Drive or Reverse.
  3. If Drive and Reverse are active at the same time, the controller goes to neutral.
Recommendation

Use a 3-position toggle switch for Drive and Reverse: centre position = neutral, end positions = Drive and Reverse.

5.2Brake Vacuum Booster#

The controller can run the vacuum pump of the brake booster. Connect the vacuum sensor to the controller and the pump through a relay.

The sensor voltage thresholds that switch the pump on and off are set in the web configurator on ECU → Brake (values are entered in mV).

6Power Relays (Contactors)#

Choose power relays with ratings close to those used in the Nissan Leaf.

Tesla contactors are not suitable

They have a high coil holding current and need an economiser. Similar contactors with a built-in current-reduction circuit exist — those can be used.

Wire cross-sections in the diagram:

Wire Cross-section Purpose
Power 35 mm² Main traction battery cables
Precharge 2.5 mm² Precharge path through the 33 Ω resistor
Control 0.75 mm² Relay coils

Observe polarity when connecting the traction battery to the PDM:

7Accelerator Pedal#

The pedal signal wire connects to pin X1-B2.

Pin Function
X1-B2 Pedal signal — primary sensor
X1-A2 Pedal signal — second sensor (not used by the firmware yet)
X1-C1 +5 V pedal supply
X1-C2 Pedal ground

The signal voltage must swing within 0–5 V — check this before connecting to the controller.

Tip

If your pedal has a second sensor, wire it to X1-A2 right away.

Both resistive and Hall-effect pedals can be used.

Warning

When connecting a Hall-effect pedal, double-check the sensor supply polarity and which wire is the signal output — otherwise you can damage the sensor or the controller's 5 V regulator.

The pedal MIN and MAX positions must be set in the web configurator (see 17.2).

8BMS#

The controller supports the Chevrolet Volt Gen 1 BMS, Orion 2 and the Nissan Leaf BMS.

8.1Chevrolet Volt Gen 1#

The BMS consists of 4 satellite modules marked 1, 2/3 (two modules) and 4. With the satellites the battery can be split into up to four separate packs.

Note

Satellites 2/3 have a jumper that sets the satellite's position in the battery. Without it the satellite will not work.

The black connector on a satellite is the interface connector. We recommend wiring CAN and power as shown in the diagram rather than through the Volt factory harness, where wires pass through the satellites in a daisy chain, which makes diagnostics harder.

The orange connectors on the satellites are for the cell balancing wires and temperature sensors. This BMS requires NTC 10 kΩ temperature sensors.

There are two connector types: 12-cell (satellites 2/3 have only this type) and 6-cell (found on satellites 1 and 4).

Note

The satellite sequence can be changed, but the cell map will then show positions incorrectly.

8.2Nissan Leaf (ZE0 / AZE0)#

The Nissan Leaf AZE0 and ZE0 BMS can be used (ZE1 is being tested). The BMS connects over CAN:

Configuration CAN-H CAN-L
Without CHAdeMO X1-A4 X1-B4
With CHAdeMO X1-A5 X1-B5

The original temperature sensors and the current sensor must also be connected to the BMS. The interlocks can be left out.

The Leaf battery connects to the controller through its LB1 connector:

LB1 Goes to
5 +12 V permanent
4, 31 +12 V from the IGN relay
1 / 2 CAN-H X1-A4 / CAN-L X1-B4 (with CHAdeMO — X1-A5 / X1-B5)
17 X2-A4 — "+" contactor coil (SYSTEM MAIN RELAY 1)
14 X2-A3 — "−" contactor coil (SYSTEM MAIN RELAY 2)
11 X2-B4 — pre-charge relay coil
6, 7, 8, 10, 13, 16 Ground

The contactors and the pre-charge relay sit in the battery junction box, so the separate power relays of section 6 are not needed — the ECU drives the stock ones from the same outputs.

The stock Leaf current sensor (LB5) stays connected to the LBC: G — ground (LBC 15), V — sensor supply (LBC 9), S — signal (LBC 10).

Note

The diagrams are for the AZE0 BMS; other versions differ slightly.

8.3Orion 2#

Supported by the controller. Detailed documentation will be added in future revisions.

8.4JK BMS (satellites)#

The controller uses JK-DZ08-B1A24S active balancers as BMS satellites. Each balancer measures its own group of cells and, when the controller asks, sends the cell voltages and its temperature over CAN.

Parameter Value
Bus CAN1: CAN-H X1-A4, CAN-L X1-B4, 250 kbps
Satellites Up to 5 supported (addresses 1–5); the diagram shows an example of 4 satellites × 24 cells = 96
Cells 2–24 per satellite, 112 in total at most
Polling The controller polls addresses 1–5 in turn, each one every 0.5 s

The controller takes the pack voltage as the sum of all cell voltages, and the over-discharge and overcharge protections work on the lowest and highest cell voltage (the cell voltage thresholds are set on the BMS → Parameters page).

What the controller does not do:

  • It does not control balancing. The balancing threshold and current, the balancing on/off switch and the cell count are stored in the balancer itself; the controller only sends the satellites a data request. The balancing settings on the BMS → Parameters page have no effect on JK balancers.
  • It does not limit current by temperature. The controller receives each satellite's temperature, but there is no protection based on it.
  • It gets no pack current from JK. The balancer does not measure current, so JK-BMS always needs the LEM CAB-500 current sensor on the same bus (see below).
Warning

JK-BMS works on CAN1 only. If CHAdeMO type is set to Internal (CAN1), CAN1 is handed over to CHAdeMO and the JK satellites are not polled; unlike the other BMS types, JK has no fallback to CAN2. Do not use this CHAdeMO type with JK-BMS.

Wiring

The diagram shows a 96-cell battery as an example: 4 satellites with 24 cells each. The controller supports up to 5 satellites — a fifth one connects to the same bus in the same way.

  • The CAN bus goes to the RS485/CAN connector on the balancer's front edge (3 contacts: G, A/H, B/L). Connect A/H (CAN-H) of every satellite to X1-A4 and B/L (CAN-L) to X1-B4, using twisted-pair wire. Contact G is left unconnected.
  • Run the bus as one line from the controller to the farthest satellite, with a short stub to each satellite.
  • The controller does not supply 12 V to the satellites: each balancer is powered from its own group through the PWR pin (P2-11), connected to the group positive. Per the JK documentation the balancer supply is 40–100 V, and PWR may go to the positive of any cell from the 13th to the 24th. For 24 NMC cells (up to 100.8 V), connect PWR to the positive of cell 23.
  • Balancing leads: connector P1 — GND (group negative) and B1–B14, connector P2 — B15–B24 and PWR. Each lead Bn goes to the positive of cell n of its group, in order, with no gaps.
  • Next to it is the TEMP connector (2 contacts, − and +) for the supplied temperature sensor; it is not wired to the controller.
Note

The satellites are connected to different sections of the traction battery. Before joining them into one CAN bus with the controller, make sure from the JK documentation that the balancer's CAN interface is galvanically isolated from the cells.

Addresses and cell numbering

  • Give every satellite its own address from 1 to 5. Addresses must not repeat: the reply's CAN ID equals the address, and two balancers with the same address would answer at the same time.
  • The controller does not poll addresses above 5.
  • The CAN protocol has no command to change the address — it is set on the balancer itself; see the JK documentation for how.

The controller numbers the cells by address: first come the cells of satellite 1, then those of satellite 2, and so on. Each satellite adds as many cells as it has detected itself; a skipped address leaves no gap in the numbering. For example, four satellites with 24 cells each give cell numbers 1–24, 25–48, 49–72 and 73–96.

Assign the addresses in the order of the groups along the battery — the cell map in the web configurator will then match the physical cell layout.

Note

If a satellite detects fewer cells than are connected (for example, because of a broken balancing lead), the cell numbers of all following satellites shift and the total cell count drops.

Termination resistors

CAN1 must be terminated with two 120 Ω resistors, one at each end of the bus. The controller already has a 120 Ω resistor built in on every CAN channel, so none is needed at the controller. Fit the second 120 Ω at the far end of the bus — at the farthest satellite. If the device at the far end already has a built-in terminator, no separate resistor is needed there.

Check: with the power off and the bus connected, measure the resistance between X1-A4 and X1-B4:

Resistance Meaning
≈ 60 Ω Correct — two terminators
≈ 120 Ω One terminator missing
≈ 40 Ω or less One terminator too many

Current sensor

With JK-BMS the pack current is measured only by the LEM CAB-500 sensor — it is required. The sensor connects to the same CAN1 bus as the satellites (see 9.2).

On the BMS → Parameters page, set Current sens type to CAB-500, then press Train (the CAB-500 Training row): the controller finds the sensor and switches it to the JK bus speed, 250 kbps.

Note

The CAB 500-C/SP5-012 sensor has a built-in 120 Ω terminator; the other CAB-500 versions do not. Take this into account when checking the bus resistance.

Web configurator settings

  1. ECU → Settings: set Type BMS to JK-BMS and press Write. Check the current value. CAN1 switches to 250 kbps immediately.
  2. BMS → Parameters: set Cells in pack to the total number of cells across all satellites. The controller derives the pack voltage limit for overcharge protection from it.
  3. BMS → Parameters: set the cell voltage thresholds and the current sensor type.

Checks after power-up

  • Before power-up: resistance between X1-A4 and X1-B4 ≈ 60 Ω.
  • BMS → Cells: all cell voltages are non-zero, numbers follow the addresses, and the last filled cell matches the total cell count.
  • BMS → Parameters: the pack voltage matches a multimeter reading, and the lowest and highest cell voltages are plausible.
  • The current changes under load and has the correct sign; for CAB-500 the direction is changed with the Toggle button in the Sensor direction row.
Note

The BMS → Cells page shows cells 1–96; cells 97–112 are not visible in the web configurator.

Warning

If a satellite does not answer for 35 s, the controller sets its cell voltages to zero (0 V on the cell map) and no longer counts them in the lowest and highest cell voltage, and the pack voltage drops by their sum. Driving is not blocked. The exception is the satellite holding cell 1: a zero voltage on that cell is treated as over-discharge and stops the car. Cells showing 0 V on the map indicate a lost satellite.

9Current Sensor#

The controller works with two current sensor types: the analog LEM DHAB (Chevrolet Volt) and the CAN sensor LEM CAB 500. The type is chosen in the web configurator: BMS → Parameters → Current sens type. The sensor can be placed anywhere inside the battery before the power relays.

9.1Chevrolet Volt Current Sensor (LEM DHAB)#

9.2LEM CAB 500 Current Sensor#

The LEM CAB 500 (CAB 500-C series) is a galvanically isolated fluxgate current sensor with a digital CAN output. A battery power cable is passed through the sensor's opening. Nominal range is ±500 A, total error 0.3 % at 25 °C, offset below 10 mA. The sensor sends the measured current by itself in frame 0x3C2 every 10 ms, and the controller receives it on the BMS bus — CAN1 — in parallel with the BMS.

The controller works with the current in whole amperes: charge current (including regeneration) is positive, discharge current is negative. The controller counts the battery charge from this value and switches on the brake light during regeneration.

Note

The controller reads the CAB 500 only when CAN1 serves the BMS: Type BMS set to Volt Gen 1, Leaf, Orion 2, VW ID or JK-BMS. With Type BMS "Deye HV" or "OFF", or with CHAdeMO type "Internal (CAN1)", the sensor is not read. For Deye HV select the current sensor type "In BMS" — the BMS itself reports the current.

Wiring

  • CAN-H and CAN-L — twisted pair to the CAN1 bus, in parallel with the BMS: X1-A4 → pin B (CAN-H), X1-B4 → pin A (CAN-L).
  • Supply — +12 V from the IGN relay to pin D (Uc). Operating range 8…16 V, consumption 40…160 mA. The sensor has no sleep mode, so do not feed it from permanent +12 V.
  • Ground — to pin C, common with the ECU ground.
  • Connector on the sensor — TE 1565749; the mating harness plug is TE 1473672-1.
  • Termination. Each end of the CAN1 bus needs a 120 Ω resistor between CAN-H and CAN-L. The controller end already has 120 Ω built in. The CAB 500 has no built-in terminator (except the CAB 500-C/SP5-012 version), so if the sensor is at the far end of the bus, fit the 120 Ω next to it.
  • Required with JK-BMS. JK balancers do not measure current, so with JK-BMS (see 8.4) the CAB 500 is always needed.

Mounting

  • Pass one battery power cable through the Ø24.2 mm opening — either the positive or the negative. Location — as for any current sensor: inside the battery, before the power relays.
  • The sensor is fixed through two Ø6.5 mm holes (63.5 mm between centres). Versions SP2 and SP5 are fixed with plastic rivets, maximum load 70 N. SP1 and SP10 have metal inserts for M6 screws (8 N·m), SP7 and SP77 for M4 (2 N·m).
  • The positive current direction Ip on the LEM drawing is through the opening from the label side towards the connector side. The sensor may face either way: the current sign is corrected in the configurator (see "Checking the current direction" below).
Danger — high voltage

Fit the sensor and route the power cable through its opening only with the traction battery de-energised.

Setup in the web configurator

  1. Open ECU → Settings, set Type BMS and press Write. Training (below) sets the sensor to the bitrate of exactly this BMS, so set the BMS type first.
  2. On BMS → Parameters, in the Current sens type row select CAB-500 and press Write. Make sure the current value has changed to "CAB-500". The CAB-500 Training and Sensor direction rows then become active.

The sensor must run at the same bitrate as the BMS:

Type BMS CAN1 and sensor bitrate
Volt Gen 1 125 kbit/s
JK-BMS 250 kbit/s
Leaf, Orion 2, VW ID 500 kbit/s

The factory bitrate of the CAB 500-C/SP5 is 500 kbit/s, of the CAB 500-C/SP5-001 250 kbit/s. If it already matches the BMS bitrate, training only confirms it.

CAB 500 training

Training looks for the sensor on the bus at 500, 250 and 125 kbit/s. If its bitrate differs from the BMS bitrate, the controller writes the new bitrate into the sensor, restarts it and checks that the sensor answers at the new bitrate.

  1. The car must be stationary and not in drive mode: the controller receives no BMS data during training.
  2. Switch the ignition on. The sensor must be connected and powered.
  3. Disconnect the BMS from the CAN1 bus (open its CAN-H and CAN-L) — only the CAB 500 must remain on the bus.
  4. On BMS → Parameters, in the CAB-500 Training row press Train and confirm the prompt "Disconnect BMS from CAN1 bus! Leave only the CAB-500 sensor. Continue?".
  5. Watch the status field. SCAN_500K → SCAN_250K → SCAN_125K — searching for the sensor (up to 1.5 s per bitrate). WRITE_BAUD → RESET → VERIFY → RESTORE — writing the bitrate, restart and check. The whole procedure takes up to 10 s.
  6. Wait for the result and reconnect the BMS.
Status Meaning
OK Bitrate changed, the sensor answers at the new bitrate
ALREADY_OK The sensor already runs at the BMS bitrate, nothing changed
ERR_NOT_FOUND The sensor was not found at any bitrate — check the supply, CAN-H/CAN-L and that the BMS is disconnected
ERR_UDS_FAIL The sensor did not confirm writing the new bitrate
ERR_VERIFY After the restart the sensor does not answer at the new bitrate

After any result the controller returns CAN1 to the BMS bitrate. Training can be started again.

Checking the current direction

  1. With no load, Current on BMS → Parameters should be about 0 A.
  2. While discharging (driving, a load switched on) the current must be negative; while charging and regenerating it must be positive.
  3. If the sign is the other way round, press Toggle in the Sensor direction row. The status switches between "Normal" and "Reverse" and is stored in the controller's memory. There is no need to turn the sensor round.
Warning

Check the current sign before the first drive and the first charge. With a wrong sign the controller counts the battery charge the wrong way and switches the brake light on at the wrong time.

10Cooling System#

A liquid cooling system is required for the powertrain to work properly.

Pump and fan switch-on temperatures are set in the web configurator on ECU → Settings. The controller can run the fan at two speeds:

  • full;
  • reduced — through a power-limiting resistor.

The fan can also be driven by an external PWM controller (without the resistor).

11Brake Light (Regeneration)#

The controller can switch on the brake light during regenerative braking. To do this, install a relay in parallel with the brake pedal switch.

Feed the brake-light signal to pin X2-B8 so the controller can see the brake pedal being pressed.

12CHAdeMO#

If the PDM has a CHAdeMO port, its internal power contactors (CHAdeMO Power Relay + and −) can be used by running separate wires from them. If the PDM has no CHAdeMO port, two additional power contactors must be installed.

The Enable Relay is installed separately regardless of the PDM version. It does not need to be high-power — only strong enough to switch the power contactor coils.

DC polarity

Pin 5 is DC−, pin 6 is DC+: on the vehicle inlet (front view) DC− is on the left, DC+ on the right. The diagram in earlier revisions of this manual showed DC+ and DC− on the inlet the other way round. Before the first charge, check with a continuity tester that inlet pin 6 goes to the CHAdeMO "+" contactor and pin 5 to the "−" contactor.

13Display#

The display controller sits on CAN0 Powertrain and reads the warning-lamp states through its own inputs; it drives a Nextion touch display.

13.1Display Controller#

13.2Nextion Intelligent Display#

The display connects to the controller's X2 connector with four wires: +5 V supply, ground and the serial port (controller TX to display RX, RX to TX).

The controller works with the Nextion Intelligent 7″ and 5″ displays. Dimensions and mounting holes of both:

14Selector#

To use the Leaf selector or separate momentary buttons with position backlighting, an additional selector controller is required. Like the display, it connects to the main Powertrain CAN bus; its +12 V comes from the relay that powers the ECU.

Pin X1-17 of the selector controller is the reverse-light signal (in both wiring options).

Note

Pin numbering on the selector connector itself may be mirrored. Wire according to the diagrams below — they show the connectors from the wire side. The interface connector (power and CAN) is X3; some older drawings label it X2.

14.1Leaf Selector#

14.2Momentary Buttons#

15OBD2 Diagnostics#

15.1OBD2 Connector#

An OBD2 socket must be installed for controller setup and diagnostics. Use an ELM327 v1.5 adapter (USB or Bluetooth) or an OBDLink. The web configurator does not support Wi-Fi adapters.

15.2Software#

  • E-Engines web configurator — the main tool: configuration, live parameters, cell map, firmware update. Runs in the browser, see section 16.
  • CanZE — Android app: cell map and battery temperature.
  • DDT4ALL — alternative configurator for Windows and Linux.

16Web Configurator#

The E-Engines web configurator runs in the browser at diag.electricengines.com.ua — nothing to install. Through an OBD2 adapter it reads the controller's live parameters, writes settings, saves them to a file and updates the firmware.

16.1Requirements#

  • Chrome or Edge on Windows, macOS, Linux or ChromeOS. On Android — Chrome with a Bluetooth LE adapter. Firefox, Safari and iOS browsers are not supported.
  • Adapter:
    • USB or classic Bluetooth — ELM327 v1.5 (a dual-board one is recommended) or OBDLink; connect with the BT button;
    • Bluetooth LE (vLinker, Vgate iCar Pro BLE and compatible) — with the BLE button;
    • Wi-Fi adapters are not supported.
  • After the first visit the site also works offline — you still need the adapter.

16.2Connecting#

  1. Switch the ignition on and plug the adapter into the OBD2 socket.
  2. Open the configurator. Pair a classic Bluetooth adapter in the system settings first.
  3. Press BT (USB or Bluetooth) or BLE and choose the adapter in the browser's dialog.
  4. When the connection is up, the button is highlighted and the log on the Terminal page shows "✓ Стан: Підключено" (connected). The "CAN Bus" indicator flashes yellow on every controller response.
  5. Open any page — values start updating automatically. To disconnect, press the highlighted button again.
Note

If the BT/BLE button is highlighted but the "CAN Bus" indicator stays grey, the adapter works but the controller does not answer: check the controller power and the CAN bus. Over BLE the indicator does not flash — go by the values on the pages.

16.3Configurator Pages#

Section Contents
Inverter HV voltage, status, motor and inverter temperatures, selector position, rpm, pedal position (mV), torque request. Pedal parameters and chart — see 17.2
BMS → Parameters Pack voltage, SOC, min/max cell voltage, current. Charge/discharge current limits, balancing, recuperation, cell voltage thresholds, SOC/SOH, current sensor type
BMS → Cells, Temp Map, SOC Map All cell voltages, temperatures, SOC calibration by cell voltage
ECU → Settings Inverter, BMS, selector, start button, charger and CHAdeMO types; wheel circumference; contactor ON voltage; pump and fan temperatures — see 17.3
ECU → Internal Analog input voltages, input and output states, firmware and bootloader versions
ECU → Brake Vacuum sensor, vacuum pump on/off thresholds
ECU → Cruise Control Speed, kP/kI/kD gains, chart and CSV log recording
ECU → Update Firmware update, export and import of parameters
Charging → AC, CHAdeMO, CCS Charging state, maximum AC charge current
Climate Climate system states, temperatures and pressure
Dashboard Speed / RPM display mode, turn signals, odometer and trip, clock sync
Terminal Adapter log; manual commands are sent with the Enter key

16.4Writing Parameters#

Each parameter is a row: Current Value (what the controller holds now), a field for the new value and a Write button. The value is applied and stored in the controller's memory immediately — there is no separate "save" command.

  • After writing, check the Current Value: that is what confirms the controller accepted the parameter. The "✓" in the log only means the command was sent.
  • Enter whole numbers in the unit shown in the field. Cell voltage thresholds and vacuum pump thresholds are entered in mV although they are displayed in volts; cruise gains are entered ×10 (15 = 1.5).
  • Drop-down lists always open on the first option, not on the current value — pick the option explicitly before pressing Write.
  • After changing the inverter type, restart the controller (ignition off and on).
Danger — high voltage

Change parameters only with the car stationary in P or N. Writing is not blocked while driving, and, for example, "Max torque" takes effect immediately.

16.5Saving and Restoring Settings#

On the ECU → Update page, Export Parameters reads the controller settings and downloads ecu_preset_<date>.json. Import Parameters writes every parameter from the file and reads them back for verification; the result is shown in a message and in the log.

The file contains the pedal and torque parameters, BMS and current sensor settings, inverter and selector types, temperatures, thresholds and cruise control. Charger type, CHAdeMO type, cell count, SOC map and dashboard settings are not included.

Warning

Importing does not ask for confirmation and does not check which controller the file came from. The SOC charge counter (Ah) is restored to its value at export time as well.

16.6Firmware Update#

  1. Put the car in P or N and stop; make sure the 12 V supply is stable. USB is preferable.
  2. On ECU → Update, click the file area and choose the firmware file (.ota) from E-Engines.
  3. Leave Update target at Application (FLASH0).
  4. Press Upload Firmware and confirm. Flashing takes about 6–15 min over USB or 15–30 min over BLE.
  5. Do not close, reload or hide the tab: in a background tab the browser slows the upload down.

An application update leaves the bootloader untouched, so a failed upload can simply be repeated.

Bootloader

Choose Bootloader (FLASH1) only when E-Engines asks you to: losing power while the bootloader is written leaves the controller unusable, with USB-only recovery.

17Initial Setup#

Once all wiring is connected and carefully checked (make sure no connector is pinned mirrored), proceed with the setup.

17.1Start-up Procedure#

Step 1. Power checks (before connecting the controller to the car)

  • Permanent +12 V on pin X1-A8 relative to X1-A7 (ground).
  • +12 V from the ignition switch on pin X1-C8.
  • Charge inlet without a gun: resistance between X1-B7 and X1-A7 is 4.7 kΩ or 2.7 kΩ (depending on inlet type).
  • Charge inlet with the gun plugged in: resistance between X1-B7 and X1-A7 is infinite (OL).

Step 2. Wake-up and sleep checks

  • Connect the controller to the car.
  • Turn the ignition on — power appears on X1-B8, the IGN relay closes.
  • Turn the ignition off and wait 10 s — power on X1-B8 disappears, the IGN relay opens.
  • Check wake-up and sleep by plugging and unplugging the AC charging gun.

Step 3. Configuration in the web configurator

Danger — high voltage

Do not continue without configuring the controller — the motor may spin at full speed or not spin at all!

  • Connect to the controller with the web configurator (16.2).
  • ECU → Settings: set the inverter, BMS and selector types and the other parameters (17.3).
  • Inverter: motor and inverter temperatures, no inverter error.
  • Charging → AC Charging: PDM module temperature.
  • Selector: the position must change on the Inverter page.
  • Pedal: Pedal position (mV) on the Inverter page must rise as you press the pedal.

Step 4. Power relay and battery polarity checks

  1. Disconnect the traction battery from the powertrain (pull the service disconnect).
  2. Connect a voltmeter to the battery output after the contactors.
  3. Press Start — the voltmeter must show voltage of the correct polarity.
  4. The controller enters protection mode and reports a precharge error — this is expected.
  5. Restart the controller (let it go to sleep and switch it on again).
  6. Repeat the test measuring resistance across the positive contactor with a multimeter:
    • before start — infinite;
    • at start — 30–50 Ω;
    • after one second — 0 Ω.

17.2Accelerator Pedal Setup#

The pedal parameters are on the Inverter page, recuperation is on BMS → Parameters. Pedal position is the pedal signal voltage in millivolts; the live value is shown in the Pedal position row.

Parameter Description
Pedal MIN position, mV Where traction starts. Below it is the regeneration zone
Pedal MAX position, mV Where "Max torque" is reached
Pedal position in calibration point, mV The break point of the curve: two linear segments before and after it
Torque in calibration point, % Torque at the calibration point as a percentage of "Max torque"
Not pressed pedal position, mV How many millivolts below the MIN position full regeneration is reached. This is an offset, not an absolute pedal position
Torque while pedal not pressed, Nm Torque added to the request in D and R (creep); 0 = off
Max torque, Nm Torque at the MAX position and beyond
Recuperation, Nm (BMS → Parameters) Full regeneration torque. Works in D only and ramps from 0 at 300 rpm to the full value at 1000 rpm

Setup order:

  1. Without touching the pedal, note the Pedal position reading; then press the pedal to the floor and note it again.
  2. Set Pedal MIN position above the released reading: the span between them becomes the regeneration zone — the wider it is, the more gradually regeneration fades as you press. Set Pedal MAX position slightly below the fully pressed reading.
  3. Set Not pressed pedal position to the difference between the MIN position and the released reading.
  4. Use the calibration point to tune the sensitivity at the start of the pedal travel, then set "Max torque" and "Recuperation".
Warning

Do not set "Not pressed pedal position" lower than the difference from step 3: the firmware does not clamp regeneration, and with the pedal released it would exceed the set value.

17.3Controller Configuration#

After the pedal is set up, open ECU → Settings and check every parameter.

Parameter Description
Wheel circumference Wheel circumference in mm (used for the speed calculation)
Contactor ON voltage, V The main contactor will not close if the inverter voltage after precharge is below this value — protection against a broken power wire or precharge resistor
Type selector Button — toggle switch or buttons on the controller inputs (5.1); CAN — separate selector controller (14); CAN inverted — the same with D and R swapped; PSA
Type start button With or without fixation (latching / momentary)
Type inverter Leaf AZE0, ZE0, ZE1 or Tesla M3 — select exactly the one installed. Restart the controller after changing it
Charger type Leaf PDM, Tesla PCS or OFF
CHAdeMO type OFF, internal (CAN1 or CAN3) or external CHAdeMO controller
Pump start temperature, °C See section 10
Fan ON temperature, °C Separately for high and low speed
Type BMS OFF, Volt Gen 1, Leaf, Orion 2, VW ID, JK-BMS, Deye HV

18FAQ / Troubleshooting#

The web configurator does not connect to the adapter

  • Use Chrome or Edge; Firefox, Safari and iOS are not supported.
  • Pair a classic Bluetooth adapter in the system settings first and connect with BT. A Bluetooth LE adapter connects with BLE.
  • Wi-Fi adapters are not supported.
  • The adapter must be ELM327 v1.5 compatible (a dual-board one is recommended) or an OBDLink. The error reason is shown in the log on the Terminal page.

Values do not update, the "CAN Bus" indicator is grey

The adapter is connected but has no CAN communication with the controller. Possible causes:

  • no power to the controller;
  • CAN bus wired incorrectly (CAN-H and CAN-L swapped);
  • controller fault.

All voltages from the BMS = 0 V

The controller does not see the BMS. Check the CAN bus wiring and the BMS power supply.

One cell reads much higher and its neighbour much lower

Most likely a poor balancing-wire contact with the cell. If it happens under load — a poor contact in the power busbars between cells. Check every connection in the battery.

The motor whines but does not turn

With the original gearbox, check that it is not locked: turn both driven wheels in the same direction. If they don't turn, rotate the parking-lock shaft counter-clockwise.

The motor turns only in reverse

This happens when a ZE0 inverter is installed but a different inverter type is selected in the controller settings.

The car briefly accelerates or regenerates by itself while driving

Seen with resistive pedals: over time the resistor tracks wear and give an unstable voltage. Solution: replace the pedal.

The traction battery contactors weld

  1. Check the contactor wiring.
  2. Check the precharge resistor value.
  3. Check the battery activation voltage parameter (above 200 V) in the configurator — it protects against a failed relay or precharge resistor.

The DC-DC converter in the PDM burned out

A ground fault (especially when the traction battery negative is tied to the 12 V system negative) can destroy the PDM.

Danger — high voltage

Always check the insulation resistance of the traction battery to the chassis.
